limits: Selected Linear has original forward and pre-node inputs, immediate post-node inputs, raw DX/DW/DB, converted, accumulated and backward-return gradients in independent device snapshots.
Host enqueue order and per-stream FIFO do not establish total causality across streams. Copies, reductions and longer storage lifetimes perturb scheduling.
Entire backing stores preserve offsets, padding and aliases, but early bucket snapshots certify the selected logical view only; neighboring slots can have concurrent writers.
Flags are resolved after actual autograd.backward return, before clipping and the explicit optimizer. Sparse fused updates may already occur inside backward.
A fault or explicitly requested finite step saves the retained frame without rerunning any producer; this is not a complete model/optimizer/allocator replay.

All three STU layers retain the established 42 scalar endpoints. Layer2 projection backward additionally retains its actual pristine x/w/dz, post-call x/w/dz and raw DX/DW/DB; recomputed forward operations and residual additions remain uncaptured.
The public triton_addmm_bwd backward currently calls native torch.sum and torch.mm; this capture does not assert which BLAS implementation ran or certify actual internal operand reads.

Three input byte-integrity flags compare complete backing stores. Full pre-call input and joint post-call input/output observations preserve aliases within an observation and remain independent across observations.

A first nonfinite/extreme or input-mutation flag saves the already-retained call after the entire backward returns. Output fault location and input continuity remain evidence, not a backend root-cause certificate.
Use split_capture to pass the Linear-only payload to its existing replay validator; the projection frame has its own provenance and schema.
Combined finite controls do not establish isolated causality or a complete training fix.
The actual process uses cap256, weighted-LN BN1 and 1 KiB hipBLASLt workspace; kernel selection varies with shape.

Scalar endpoints and batches are retained references, not new boundary snapshots. Their device bytes are observed by the existing save path after the original flush; exact CPU rows preserve what that flush returned.
Retaining tiny scalar storages and batches extends their lifetime. No extra reductions, stacks, stream joins or boundary host readbacks are introduced.
The original scan order, flag rules and first flagged trigger are unchanged. This capture alone does not detect every finite scalar mismatch or identify a faulty reduction, stack, transfer or writer.

Only the selected BF16 Contraction_l_Ailk_Bjlk_Cijk_Dijk catalog matching table redirects 103 to 102 across varying sizes. Both solution definitions and all native objects remain unchanged. This is not a global VGPR policy or a validated training fix.

frame_file.note: Path/size verified only here; root owns full payload hashing and tensor audit.

source_semantics: Frozen worker checks private catalog and required/absent controls before and after bootstrap; archive records the same identity before writing context.
Frozen deferred flush resolves each queued scan once after actual backward return, marks any nonfinite/extreme or expected-zero mismatch, and saves/stops on the first flagged scan.
Requested finite step1 traverses the unchanged diagnostic save path; step2 is checked but has no requested full-frame save.
Outcome bounded_complete requires trainer SystemExit42 at requested global step2; wrapper catches that bounded exit and launcher performs its final frozen-source hash check.
limitations: This audit reads context, source archives, JSON event records and log files. It does not load or scan saved frame tensor data; parent/root own scalar, tensor and native-trace audits.

Finite/unflagged here describes recorded monitored floating summaries and integrity flags, not every model value or an external recomputation of reductions. Twelve integer mask/index metadata records per step are intentionally unscanned with null extrema.

Context omits alternate-selector keys and LD_PRELOAD/trace variables. Their requested values are in the pinned launcher; selector absence is enforced by the pinned worker bootstrap checks. Native dispatch requires root trace audit.
Worker context git_head is null. Exact current/archive/source hashes establish the reviewed source identity; a worker git commit is not inferred.
No outer-session terminal/reap sidecar is included here. Bounded completion is supported by outcome, event lifecycle, completion log and both launcher hash passes; root owns process lifecycle.
Two finite training steps do not establish long-run correctness, a complete fix or VGPR count as causal.
